hook.line: Rain hammers the window of the café and Don Hernando can't believe it. When a verb itself is what amazes you, Spanish has a short way to say so.

examples.en: He knows so much about coffee!

rule:
To be amazed at an action, put *cómo* or *cuánto* straight in front of the verb. *Cómo* is about how it happens: *¡Cómo canta!* *Cuánto* is about how much: *¡Cuánto sabe!* Before a verb, *cuánto* never changes. Before a noun it agrees: *¡Cuántas cosas!*
Nothing goes between the exclamation word and the verb, so the subject comes after: *¡Cómo canta esa mujer!*
For an adjective or adverb, use *qué* instead: *¡Qué bien canta!*
smallPrint: Teachers call these exclamatives: question words used to express surprise instead of asking.

options: She asks how that woman sings.
The neighborhood has changed so much!
How much has the neighborhood changed?

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *cómo* or *qué*, then type the whole sentence: ¡___ llueve! (It's really pouring!)
yourTurn.why: *Llueve* is a verb, so *cómo* goes right in front of it.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *cuántos* or *cuántas*, then type the whole sentence: ¡___ cosas han cambiado! (So many things have changed!)
yourTurn.why: Before a noun, *cuánto* agrees with it, and *cosas* is feminine plural.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: That woman can really sing!
yourTurn.why: The subject waits until after the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Hernando knows so much about coffee!
yourTurn.why: *Cuánto* is about amount, and it stays the same before a verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I miss Rosa so much!
yourTurn.why: Same pattern: the exclamation word, then the verb, then the rest.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it an exclamation about the verb: *Hernando baila muy bien.* becomes: Hernando can really dance!
yourTurn.why: Drop *muy bien* and let *cómo* carry the surprise.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it an exclamation about the amount: *Vale trabaja mucho.* becomes: Vale works so much!
yourTurn.why: *Cuánto* replaces *mucho* and moves in front of the verb.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Nothing goes between *cómo* and the verb, so the subject comes after it.
Almost. With an adverb or adjective, use *qué*; *cómo* goes straight onto a verb.
Almost. Before a noun, *cuánto* agrees with it: *cosas* is feminine plural.

personal: Think of someone you know who impresses you. Say it with *¡Cómo…!* or *¡Cuánto…!*
